answers.reason: The elected student representative represents the students of a single faculty, not the whole university.
Budget allocation across the university is not the domain of a faculty student representative.
Selecting candidates for professorships is separate from the student representative's single place of participation.
Although elected for the faculty, the student representative's specific domain is teaching and degree programmes in the study commission.
As the elected spokesperson for the faculty's students, their primary place is the body preparing changes to degree programmes and advising on teaching.
Individual examination matters and administrative records fall outside the student representative's single committee.
Research funding decisions do not concern the elected student representative.
Every member participates in only one body, and the student representative sits on the study commission rather than this working group.
Choosing laboratory equipment is unrelated to the student representative's role.
Planning the orientation week is for regular students, whereas the elected representative sits in the formal study commission.
